blocks.text: Imagine a database where changing a single piece of information requires updating multiple records. This is inefficient and error-prone. Functional dependencies help us design databases to avoid such problems.

blocks.markdown: Functional dependencies are a fundamental concept in database normalization. They describe relationships between attributes in a relational database and are crucial for designing tables that minimize redundancy and update anomalies.

blocks.title: Functional Dependency
blocks.text: A functional dependency, denoted as $X \rightarrow Y$, exists between two sets of attributes $X$ and $Y$ in a relation if, for any two tuples, whenever the tuples agree on the attributes in $X$, they must also agree on the attributes in $Y$.

blocks.markdown: In simpler terms, if you know the value of $X$, you can determine the value of $Y$. This is crucial in ensuring that data is stored efficiently and consistently.

blocks.title: Identifying Functional Dependencies
blocks.prompt: Consider a relation with attributes: StudentID, CourseID, and Grade. Identify a functional dependency.

steps.text: Examine the attributes and their relationships. StudentID uniquely identifies a student.
Each student can have a unique Grade for a specific CourseID. Thus, (StudentID, CourseID) uniquely determines Grade.

blocks.answer: The functional dependency is (StudentID, CourseID) \rightarrow Grade.

blocks.markdown: Functional dependencies can lead to anomalies if not properly managed. Anomalies are problems that arise when inserting, updating, or deleting data.

blocks.title: Anomalies
blocks.text: Insertion, update, and deletion anomalies can occur if functional dependencies are not properly addressed in database design.

blocks.title: Understanding Anomalies
blocks.prompt: Explain an update anomaly in the context of a student database with attributes: StudentID, Name, and Course.

steps.text: Suppose a student's name changes. In a poorly designed database, every record with that StudentID must be updated.
If one record is missed, data inconsistency occurs, leading to an update anomaly.

blocks.answer: An update anomaly occurs when changing a student's name requires updating multiple records, risking inconsistency.

blocks.markdown: To manage functional dependencies, we often compute the closure of an attribute set. The closure helps determine all attributes functionally determined by a given set.

blocks.title: Closure of an Attribute Set
blocks.text: The closure of a set of attributes $X$, denoted $X^+$, is the set of all attributes that are functionally determined by $X$.

rows: Occurs when certain attributes cannot be inserted into the database without the presence of other attributes.
Occurs when a change in one attribute requires changes in multiple rows.
Occurs when deleting a record results in the loss of other valuable data.
